**About Us:**

Since 1991, Pajaro Valley Prevention and Student Assistance (PVPSA) has supported the health and well-being of youth and families throughout the Pajaro Valley. The organization provides comprehensive health education, mental health services, substance use prevention and intervention, and direct counseling to students and families, including those served by the Pajaro Valley Unified School District (PVUSD), the largest school district in Santa Cruz County and extending into North Monterey County.

PVPSA pioneered a dedicated nonprofit-agency model built around its unique partnership with the local school district. Over more than three decades, the organization has expanded its partnerships across cities, counties, and public and private organizations to address critical community issues including substance use, gang prevention, mental health, school expulsions, and educational outcomes.

At the heart of PVPSA’s work is a commitment to prevention and early intervention. Using an upstream public health approach, the organization works to address the social determinants of health and strengthen community health and wellness through direct services, prevention and intervention programs, community partnerships, and health-related public policy advocacy. **About The Newark Museum of Art**:

*We acknowledge the traditional homelands of the Lenape, also known as the Delaware, upon which The Newark Museum of Art resides.*

We welcome everyone with inclusive experiences that spark curiosity and foster community.

Founded in 1909 and located in New Jersey, The Newark Museum of Art (NMOA) is the state's largest museum and ranks twelfth nationally in terms of collection size. Global and diasporic, the collection includes more than 130,000 artworks, as well as significant holdings of science and natural history. From the ancient world to the art of today, NMOA boasts exceptional quality and depth in the Arts of Global Africa; Arts of Global Asia, featuring a renown Tibetan collection and Buddhist altar; Arts of the Americas, with particular strength in Native American art; Arts of the Ancient Mediterranean, and Decorative Arts.

Visitor-and community-centered, NMOA responds to the evolving needs and interests of the diverse publics it serves by offering exhibitions, programming, a research library, paid internships, and local and global partnerships. A four-acre campus includes the National Historic Landmark Ballantine House (1885); the Ward Carriage House (1868); the Old Stone School House (1784); and the Alice Ransom Dreyfuss Memorial Garden. NMOA has launched an era of transformation to create an engaged citizenry by reimagining the role of the art museum for the 21st century.

**Job Summary:**

* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.

* **Skills:** Strong communication, interpersonal, and project management skills with the ability to build consensus across diverse community stakeholders.

* Ensure successful transition and operational implementation of the Clubhouse model.
* Provide consistent leadership, accountability, and support to program staff.
* Maintain strong, transparent relationships with the Board of Directors, County Behavioral Health, and community partners.
* Ensure timely completion of grant reports and contract deliverables.

* Local travel within Santa Cruz County.

**Program Director-Housing and Crisis Intervention**

Based upon program and client needs, some evening (monthly shelter meeting until 10:00PM), weekend, and holiday hours are required. While we respect work life balance at Briarpatch Youth Services, we are a 24/7/365 facility and urgent matters related to shelter, youth crisis, IT, finance, or press can emerge at any time. This means that, as an exempt leadership team member, you may have a call/matter that occurs in the evening or on the weekend.

Full time
  
  
**Shift:**  
**Description:**  
The Chief Development Officer provides a new foundation to lead fund development efforts to new levels of success in support of key strategic priorities. This position provides strategic leadership to foster the charitable investment of individuals, corporations, foundations and other entities to advance the mission of Loyola Medicine through Loyola University Health System, Loyola University Stritch School of Medicine and Loyola University Niehoff School of Nursing. While the supported organizations are legally separate entities, Loyola values a donor-centered approach to engagement that will allow donors to give across a continuum to include medical education, medical research and clinical patient care. The CDO will work in close collaboration with the CEO of Loyola University Health System, the Medicine School Dean, The Nursing School Dean, the Provost for the Health Sciences Division and other senior leaders. This leader will be expected to foster a mutually respectful and collaborative relationship with Vice President for Advancement for Loyola University and university development teams.
  
  
ABOUT LOYOLA MEDICINE
  
  
Loyola Medicine, a member of Trinity Health, is a nationally ranked academic, quaternary care system based in Chicago's western suburbs. The three-hospital system includes Loyola University Medical Center (LUMC), Gottlieb Memorial Hospital, MacNeal Hospital, as well as convenient locations offering primary care, specialty care and immediate care services from nearly 2,000 physicians throughout Cook, Will and DuPage counties. Saint Joseph Health System is also part of Loyola Medicine and includes two acute care hospitals. More information about saint Joseph Health can be found atAbout Us | Saint Joseph Health System.
  
  
LUMC is a 547-licensed-bed hospital in Maywood that includes the William G. and Mary A. Ryan Center for Heart& Vascular Medicine, the Cardinal Bernardin Cancer Center, the John L. Keeley, MD, Emergency Department, a Level 1 trauma center, Illinois's largest burn center, the Nancy W. Knowles Orthopaedic Institute, a certified comprehensive stroke center, transplant center and a children’s hospital. Having delivered compassionate care for over 50 years, Loyola also trains the next generation of caregivers through its academic affiliation with Loyola University Chicago’s Stritch School of Medicine and Marcella Niehoff School of Nursing.
  
  
Established in 1961, Gottlieb Memorial Hospital is a 235-licensed-bed community hospital in Melrose Park that includes the Judd A. Weinberg Emergency Department, the Loyola Center for Metabolic Surgery and Bariatric Care, Loyola Cancer Care& Research at the Marjorie G. Weinberg Cancer Center, acute rehabilitation, a transitional care center, childcare center and fitness center. Founded in 1919, MacNeal Hospital is a 349-licensed-bed teaching hospital in Berwyn with advanced medical, surgical and psychiatric services and a 68-bed behavioral health program.
  
POSITION PURPOSE
  
  
The position will be based in Maywood, IL (Greater Chicagoland) and will require some travel throughout the city as well as within Northern Indiana to include Saint Joseph Health (part of Loyola Medicine).
  
  
Saint Joseph Health System
  
  
Saint Joseph Health System is a not-for-profit, multi-hospital health system located in North Central Indiana. Our system includes:
  
  

* 254-bed acute-care hospital at the Mishawaka Medical Center.
* 58-bed acute-care hospital at the Plymouth Medical Center.
* More than 150 providers in the Saint Joseph Physician Network.
* Community health centers and additional points of access.
* St. Paul’s with 316 suites for independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing care, rehabilitation and wellness and memory care.
* Holy Cross with 168 suites for rehabilitation and wellness and skilled nursing care.
* Trinity Tower with 84 affordable senior apartments.
* Health Insurance Services.
* VNA Home Care.

Saint Joseph Health System continues the legacy of caring for Michiana begun by the Sisters of the Holy Cross and the Poor Handmaids of Jesus Christ more than 150 years ago. Saint Joseph Health System is a Regional Ministry Organization of Trinity Health that provides compassionate, faithbased care paired with the latest in advanced medical technology and procedures.

**About the Role**

Dorchester Bay Economic Development Corporation (DBEDC) is hiring a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to lead the organization's internal management and serve as second in command. The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) sets direction and the standard for the organization and leads it externally. The COO makes that direction and standard real inside the organization by managing the six department leads, running the operating rhythm, leading executive-level projects, and translating where DBEDC is going into what it means for each department and for staff day-to-day.

The COO joins an Executive Leadership Team with two peers: the Chief Real Estate Officer, who leads real estate development and asset management, and the Chief Development and Communications Officer, who leads resource development and communications. The three Chiefs work as equals and as thought partners to one another and to the CEO. Much of DBEDC's most important work sits where their areas meet, and the COO is expected to build strong working relationships with both from the start.

Dorchester Bay is a dual-certified community development corporation and community development financial institution serving Dorchester, Roxbury, and nearby neighborhoods. We have about 30 staff, a roughly $10 million operating budget, more than 1000 units of affordable housing, and a community loan fund that finances small businesses and real estate in our neighborhoods. We are a small organization with a large footprint, and our management structure needs to catch up to our complexity.

**Why this role now:**

The Board recently adopted three strategic priorities: Expand Community Ownership and Wealth; Advance Housing as a Platform for Health; and Reframe Education as a Wealth and Power Building Tool and Prepare Residents for the Future Economy. Delivering on them requires an internal leader who can turn priorities into operating plans and hold the organization to them.

Community Engagement, Workforce Development, and Community Lending need to function as one economic stabilization and mobility engine for our neighborhoods rather than as separate lines of work.

Every senior leader currently reports to the CEO. That is too many direct reports for one person to manage well while also leading strategy, policy, the Board, enterprise finance, and external relationships. Our department leads deserve consistent executive management: clear expectations, practical coaching, direct feedback, and support in delivering results.

DBEDC is a technology-forward organization. We expect our leaders to use technology and data to work more effectively, to adopt new tools quickly, and to bring their teams along.

**What the COO owns in one year:**

* **The department leads.** The COO manages, coaches, and develops the six department leads. Every lead has outcome goals, a development plan, and a manager who follows through. The COO raises the standard of leadership across the group and works with the CEO to make the decisions necessary to ensure every department is led at the level our residents and partners deserve.

* **The operating rhythm and executive-level projects.** The COO runs the weekly, monthly, and quarterly management cadence, makes sure decisions get made and carried out, and leads the cross-department projects that require executive ownership, including those shared with real estate and development.

* **Translating direction into practice.** The COO turns the direction the CEO sets and the priorities the Board has adopted into practical operating expectations for each department: what each team is expected to deliver, how the work is organized, and how the three program departments work together as one engine.

Department leads own their departments. The Director of Operations owns administrative systems, policies, and day-to-day operations. The Controller owns accounting, controls, and compliance. Program directors own their programs and the practices that connect them. As a general rule, the COO does not backfill department-level management, stepping into a lead's work only to cover an absence. The COO also recognizes when development has run its course and a leadership change is in the organization's best interest, and leads that process fairly and decisively in partnership with People and Culture and the CEO.

**How the Leadership Team Works Together**

The CEO sets the direction and the standard, communicates where the organization is going, and carries DBEDC's relationships with the Board, funders, partners, and the public, along with enterprise financial stewardship and the organization's most consequential risk decisions. The COO presents operating financial performance to the Board's Finance Committee alongside the CEO and develops the finance function's capacity to do so directly over time. The CEO is direct, moves quickly, and holds a high bar for quality, and expects the leadership team to bring the same clarity and care to their own work.

The three Chiefs lead their areas as peers. The Chief Real Estate Officer leads real estate development and asset management. The Chief Development and Communications Officer leads resource development and communications. The COO leads internal management and the program and administrative departments. The Chiefs are expected to think together, plan together, share information freely, and resolve cross-area questions directly with one another, bringing to the CEO only what they cannot resolve or where the CEO can add value.

The work overlaps constantly. With the Chief Real Estate Officer, the COO makes sure finance supports development projects and property-level accounting across DBEDC's affiliated entities, connects workforce development to jobs created through construction and property operations, aligns community lending with small businesses that lease space in our properties, and makes sure community engagement supports community input on new development.

The University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) - a global leader in health sciences - is seeking an extraordinary, strategic, and collaborative **Executive Director of Development, Neurosciences** . In this high-profile role, you will direct a dedicated frontline fundraising team and partner directly with world-class department chairs, institute directors, clinical leaders, and pioneering researchers to design and secure transformative major and principal philanthropic gifts ($250k to $10M+) across the **UCSF Weill Institute for Neurosciences** .

As a senior development strategist within the Office of University Development and Alumni Relations (UDAR), you will occupy a critical leadership position, shaping the future of neurology, neurosurgery, and psychiatry. You will bridge complex clinical priorities and visionary scientific research, converting them into inspiring, high-impact donor opportunities that accelerate discoveries for neurodegenerative diseases, mental health, brain injury, and cognitive science.

**Why This Role Is Unique**

**Power a World-Renowned Ecosystem:** Drive philanthropic strategy across the prestigious UCSF Weill Institute for Neurosciences, unifying elite departments - including Neurology, Neurological Surgery, and Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences - alongside cutting-edge research centers.

* **Direct Access to Visionary Academic Leadership:** Serve as a trusted advisor and strategic partner to department chairs, institute directors, and world-renowned scientists, translating complex clinical and basic science visions into compelling philanthropic narratives.
* **High-Impact, Transformative Philanthropy:** Secure visionary gifts that directly accelerate clinical breakthroughs, expand patient access, fund high-risk/high-reward research, and empower the next generation of neuroscience leaders.
* **Senior Strategic & Team Leadership:** Direct, mentor, and elevate a high-performing frontline fundraising team while serving as a key strategist on UDAR leadership bodies, including Frontline Leaders and Executive Team spaces.
* **Unrivaled Collaborative Environment:** Join one of the nation's premier academic development organizations, built on a culture of deep partnership, intellectual curiosity, and shared accomplishment.
  

**Desired Mindset & Competencies**

* **Intellectual Curiosity & Passion for Neuroscience:** A genuine fascination with brain health, clinical innovation, and biomedical research, paired with the ability to translate complex medical concepts into inspiring donor opportunities.
* **Strategic Agility & Political Acumen:** Demonstrated expertise navigating complex organizations, aligning diverse stakeholder interests, and managing multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously.
* **Collaborative Leadership & Team Orientation:** High emotional intelligence, a team-first mindset, and a commitment to growing talent, celebrating collective wins, and fostering a supportive, high-performing environment.
  

* note: Salary commensurate with internal equity based on education, scope, and experience

Our success comes from the combined talents of many roles: frontline fundraisers who build transformative partnerships with donors; alumni relations professionals who nurture lasting connections with the UCSF community; writers and designers who help tell the university’s story; researchers and analysts who provide critical insights; and operations and information systems experts who keep us running smoothly.
